subject: Day 12: lochia tapering; prep for the first growth spurt
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 12. The first common growth spurt is two to three days out. It looks like sudden, near-constant feeding for 24-48 hours. Knowing it is coming is half the work — it is a normal calibration, not a supply failure.

Action items
- Read ahead on cluster feeding so the spurt does not read as a problem; resist supplementing reflexively if breastfeeding.
- Stock the kitchen and freezer for the spurt window — feeding marathons leave no time to cook.
- Confirm Avi's health-insurance enrollment actually processed by calling the insurer; do not trust that the form went through. Healthcare.gov on qualifying life events: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- If the SSN has arrived, open the 529 this week. 529 plan overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/529_plan
- Continue the feeding and output log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump detaching around now; baby acne peaking; mother's lochia light and tapering.
- [low concern] Evening fussiness and a stronger need to be held.
- [monitor] Mother's mood — baby blues should be easing by the end of week two; persistence past that escalates the concern.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting with weight stagnation. Fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Build toward 15 minutes of daily tummy time across short post-feed bouts. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Hold him in front of a mirror for 30-60 seconds; he is not recognizing himself yet, but face-perception circuitry is tuning.
- Narrate your next ordinary task in full, simple sentences during an awake-alert window.
- Offer slow face-to-face time 8-12 inches away — he prefers human faces over any other pattern.

Upcoming
- Day 14-21: first growth spurt; expect a feeding-frequency surge.
- Day 14-21: complete the EPDS maternal mood screen.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; first social smiles.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete

- Reacts to loud sounds (startle, blink, stillness)
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Confirms intact hearing response. Universal newborn hearing screen catches most cases but daily observation matters.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-loud-sound/complete

- Brings hands within range of eyes and mouth
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Early body awareness. Not yet purposeful — looks like accidental discovery.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brings-hands-near-face/complete
